entries.title: P0017 October 2026 source status
entries.statement: Bizeul, Klartag and Lehec, arXiv:2610.05474v1, Theorem 1.1, claim a universal dimension-independent Poincare bound for isotropic log-concave probability measures. This is a version-specific primary-source claim. The complete proof was not independently audited for this draft, so current openness and correctness are recorded as UNKNOWN rather than inferred from the 2026-09-07 attempted-unsolved ledger label.
assumptions: No complete proof certification in this bundle

entries.title: False coordinate conditional-averaging shortcut
entries.statement: FALSE candidate: there is a universal finite K such that, for every isotropic log-concave joint law of (U,V) and every smooth f, the marginal Dirichlet energy of v -> E[f(U,V)|V=v] is at most K times the full joint Euclidean Dirichlet energy of f. This fails already for isotropic laws in dimension two.
assumptions: Euclidean gradients before and after conditioning
The proposed K is independent of the law

entries.title: Epigraph obstruction to a coordinate-averaging energy bound
entries.statement: For p>=2, take the law on R^2 with density proportional to exp(-x) on x>=|y|^p, and whiten its two coordinates to an isotropic log-concave pair (U,V). For f(u,v)=u, the full joint Dirichlet energy is 1, while the marginal Dirichlet energy of E[f|V] is D_p=p^2 Gamma(3/p) Gamma(2-1/p)/[(1+1/p) Gamma(1/p)^2], with D_p/p -> 1/3. This proves failure of a universal finite coordinate-averaging energy bound, not failure of global KLS. Author w352; independently checked by w353; further review required before theorem promotion.
assumptions: Conditional mean is taken after whitening

entries.title: False pointwise posterior covariance shortcut
entries.statement: FALSE candidate: there exist fixed t>0 and theta<1 such that every isotropic log-concave prior mu in every dimension has Cov(X|X+sqrt(t)Z=y)<=theta t I for almost every observation y, where Z is an independent standard Gaussian. A one-dimensional shifted-exponential prior disproves this pointwise assertion. This does not decide any averaged Dirichlet contraction.
assumptions: almost every observation is under the convolution law

entries.title: Shifted-exponential posterior pointwise margin obstruction
entries.statement: PROVISIONAL author result, independent referee pending: let X=Exp(1)-1 and Y=X+sqrt(t)Z for fixed t>0 and independent standard Gaussian Z. The prior is isotropic and log-concave on R. For alpha=(-1-y+t)/sqrt(t), lambda=phi(alpha)/P(Z>alpha), the posterior variance is t[1+alpha lambda-lambda^2]. As y tends to +infinity, this divided by t tends to 1 on positive-probability tail neighborhoods. Thus its essential supremum equals t and no universal theta<1 gives a pointwise posterior covariance margin. This says nothing about the averaged gradient energy contraction or KLS.

relations.rationale: Version-specific October source claim updates the dated historical P0017 open-problem label without certifying a proof.
The exact energy ratio D_p diverges as p tends to infinity for isotropic log-concave laws.
The essential supremum of posterior variance divided by t is one for this isotropic one-dimensional prior; the author result awaits independent review.
